contexts.text: They were delighted solely with internal things...

(With killing and torturing their companions) they are so delighted, that such things are their highest delights. They who have been bloodthirsty, are delighted to torture spirits... At the sight of blood... they are intensely delighted... They who have been delighted with mere pleasures... are in the highest degree delighted to stay in privies, etc.
(Good Spirits behold these objects) always with interior delight.
He who when able actually does evil, and is delighted in it, is among the infernals.

Spirits who in the bodily life had been delighted with the Word of the Lord with delight, in the other life have a certain delightful heavenly heat... The heat of those who had been somewhat delighted, when communicated to me, was like a vernal warmth... The heat of those who had been still more affected with the delight of the Lord's Word... was interior. The heat of those who had been still more affected and delighted, was still more interiorly delightful...
The heat of those who indeed had been delighted with the Word, but had not been solicitous about the understanding of it, was only in the right arm.
This delight lasted some months, but now that it has become familiar, they wonder at it no longer.
The general delight, or regnant affection (of truth separated from good) is to conquer.

In the appearances themselves there is delight; wherefore, if the Rational is deprived of appearances, it supposes that there is nothing more of delight... It is admissible for it to have delight in them.
Little children in the other life... are most highly delighted with (little children on earth).
When I read to them something from the Word, they were in the highest degree delighted; it was granted to perceive their very delight and delight... HH 322:2.
Delightful things, but not desirable ones. Signified.

Desirable and delightful things for the Divine Rational. Signified. The delights which are of good are desirable, and the pleasant things which are of truth are delightful; for the affection of good is that which desires, and then the affection of truth is that which delights.
It is the heavenly pleasantness of the Angels which flows in and causes the delight of little children (in the Word).
Thus does he see those things with which he had before been delighted, further and further removed from him.
This good then manifests itself by affection, namely, by this, that the man is affected with truth, or begins to be delighted with it...
It is otherwise with those who are in the affection of charity; these are delighted with such arcana...
Spirits especially retain those things with which they are delighted... for the things which are of delectation and love... remain...
Nothing delights the infernals except to do what is evil...
The truths with which good can be conjoined... are such as delight the intellectual sight, thus which enter into the affection...
The Angels are delighted with such a man...
It would be quite otherwise, if the mind were delighted with heavenly things more than worldly ones, for those things with which man is delighted are apprehended. Example(s).
Hence it is said that variety delights, and it is known that the delight is according to its quality.
These things can be comprehended, provided the mind is delighted with them; for delight is attended with light, because it is from love...
Into the affections (of little children there) are first insinuated such things as... are delightful.
For the sake of the truth itself, with which they are inmostly affected and delighted.
As this light enters, it also affects and delights; for whatever flows in and is received from Heaven, is attended with delight and pleasantness.
With dirt they are then delighted, in like manner as they had been in the world with riches for the sake of evil uses. Explained.
The Angels are not delighted with the external things themselves, but with the things they represent.
He who wills good to himself only, is delighted with the evils which take place with others.

Evil Spirits are eager (for these stenches), because they are for delight; for as everyone in the world has been delighted with his own evil, so after death he is delighted with the stench to which his evil corresponds.
The highest delight (of the Angels) consists in this.
They who have been delighted with the Word, in the other life receive the heat of Heaven, in which is celestial love, according to the quality and quantity of their delight from love. WH 17:3.
Uses for the support of the body, relate to its delectation, etc. Explained.
Applying nutrition to the goods of love, clothing to the truths of wisdom, habitation to Heaven, recreation and delectation to happiness of life and heavenly joy...
In proportion as (the Angels) are rational spiritual, the delectation, protection, and preservation of the state are theirs.
This delight of the Angels (in the Word) is communicated to the man, and effects consociation, and also a communication of perceptions.
The phantasies of evil Spirits are direful and cruel, delighting themselves in cruelly treating men.
They who are delighted with mensurations.
The delectation of speaking with man after death is nothing... But heavenly joy is ineffable, and in comparison with it all earthly and worldly delectations are nothing.
On a certain species of abode where they are delighted by this, that they are continually led about.
They take thence their sole delight.
With these (cruelties) they are so delighted, that they are their highest delights.
The greater the torment, the greater is their delight, which is so great with them, that they say it surpasses all delights.
They... induced a kind of washing from head to foot, with delight.
1.2. Some are delighted even to their inmosts, by manifold pleasantnesses, as paradisiacal ones...
On the punishment of those who are delighted with revenge.
The harmony is from the custom of the life, by virtue of which they have taken delight.

They have acquired a harmony in contrary things, as in contradicting, in plotting against marriage love... and, in fact, with such delight, that they suppose nothing to be more delightful. Their delights have sometimes been communicated to me...

These he obtains in abundance, and with delight, so long as he is nothing to himself... and with a perception indefinitely fuller than a man has in his own delights... When the sensation and perception of the delights from their own loves ceased.
On those who are in the delight of adultery and cruelty.
The Lord... insinuated into the Angels... affection with delight.
(The spirit) is in... wisdom and in happiness, that is, in the highest delights originating from the affections of good.

(Aristotle) thought from the delight of the affection, which reigned, and excited him to think; so that it was [characteristic] of him to think from affection, and thence the delight of the act... But his followers... [would proceed] from mere terms... to delight, which cannot exist, except from some affection, which is not [with them] the affection and thence the delight of thinking, but an external cupidity...
The philosophy of such things is of no use, except for the sake of the delight.
His pleasure consisted in this, that he was delighted in writing (books)... This was his sole pleasure and delight...
Hence it may appear with what sort of delight the most malignant Spirits are possessed.
I perceived the delight (of Cicero) when I read the prophetic Word...
The Plutonic Spirits are delighted with immense treasures of gold... because they had been such as to place all their delight in such things apart from use...
Worship from the good of love is signified by then shalt thou be delighted with the sacrifices of righteousness, and with burnt-offering ().
To be delighted greatly with the commandments of Jehovah () = to love them, thus to will and do them.
That she will then be accepted by the Lord, is signified by then shall the King be delighted with thy beauty ().
Every form delights by its varieties. Example(s).
